summary: Build outbreak investigation and surveillance reporting skills with practical tools, indicators, and templates. Enrol in advanced training today.
lede: Epidemiology and disease surveillance turn population health data into signals that support disease control and outbreak response. This training is for professionals working with surveillance data and public health reporting; it develops practical skills in defining cases, building line lists, assessing data quality, interpreting epidemic curves, and communicating findings through surveillance reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with surveillance data, outbreak signals, and public health reporting and need deeper field-level capability.
prerequisites: You should have an advanced working knowledge of public health surveillance concepts, outbreak response terminology, and basic descriptive statistics. Familiarity with case definitions, line lists, Excel or a comparable spreadsheet tool, and routine reporting processes will help you move quickly into applied work. No programming is required to complete the course, but prior exposure to biostatistical analysis or surveillance software will be useful for the practical exercises.
